f.title: Take paediatric utilisation and off-label use into account in data collection modalities
f.statement: Adverse reactions in the paediatric population need a specific evaluation, and modalities of data collection should take into account that medicines in the paediatric population have a different utilisation pattern and are often used off-label.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Adverse reactions in the paediatric population need a specific evaluation, as they may substantially 46 differ - in terms of frequency, nature, severity and presentation - from those occurring in the adult 47 population (see P.IV.A.1.). The importance of performing specific research in pharmacovigilance 48 targeting the paediatric population2 has been recognised and established, and modalities of data 49 collection should take into account that medicines in the paediatric population have a different 50 utilisation pattern and often are used off-label.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. quote re-cut to start at the sentence 'Adverse reactions in the paediatric population need a specific evaluation' so the statement is proven; 'should take into account' with no named actor; background-style sentence.

f.title: Consider organ maturation, developmental pharmacology and long-term follow-up in paediatric PV
f.statement: Aspects related to organ maturation and developmental pharmacology should be taken into account when performing pharmacovigilance activities for the paediatric population, and the value of long-term follow-up should be considered systematically.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

rows.quote: These considerations highlight the importance of taking into account aspects related to organ 115 maturation and developmental pharmacology7 when performing pharmacovigilance activities for the 116 paediatric population and imply that the value of long-term follow-up should be considered 117 systematically.

f.title: Use adult knowledge to inform paediatric risk management and adapt RMM to paediatric patients
f.statement: Knowledge gained from adults, when available, should inform data collection methods and risk minimisation tools for paediatric subjects; limitations of adult risk minimisation methods need to be appraised and some approaches should be adapted to target paediatric patients more effectively.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Discuss paediatric-specific safety topics in RMP risk identification where they lead to specific risks
f.statement: For medicinal products with a paediatric indication, a number of safety topics are of particular interest for the risk identification discussion in the RMP, and they should be discussed if they lead to possible specific risks.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force). Medicinal products with a paediatric indication.

f.title: Consider a paediatric PASS when a paediatric risk is a safety concern in the RMP
f.statement: If a specific paediatric risk is included as a safety concern in the RMP safety specification, consideration should be given to whether a paediatric PASS would be an appropriate tool to further characterise the risk.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.statement: The legal requirements and general guidance in GVP Module VI are to be followed for management and reporting of adverse reactions; ICSR reporting requirements for the paediatric population, including off-label use, are not different from adults.

f.title: Record patient age accurately in structured ICSR fields
f.statement: Patient age in ICSRs should be recorded as accurately as possible (gestational age for pre-term neonates, completed days for neonates, days or months for infants and toddlers, completed years or months for children and adolescents), and should be available in the structured ICSR data fields rather than the narrative.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Consider youth-appropriate media and parent/carer materials for additional RMM
f.statement: Younger people's media preferences (infographics, comics, video clips, social media) should be considered in preparing additional RMM; educational materials for parents/carers should be considered in some situations, e.g. for correct administration or diversion/misuse risk.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Equip HCPs to discuss risks with children and carers, including growth and long-term effects
f.statement: Safety communication and HCP educational materials should aid discussion of risks with children and their parents/carers; where applicable, advice needs to address sensitivities such as impact on growth and development, cognitive and sexual/reproductive functions and potential long-term effects.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Conduct PV per Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation 726/2004 addressing paediatric aspects
f.statement: The MAH or applicant in the EU has the legal obligation to conduct pharmacovigilance per Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 and should address paediatric-specific aspects in accordance with P.IV.B guidance, following P.IV.C.1 when operating in the EU.
f.clause: P.IV.C.1.1. Marketing authorisation holder and applicant in the EU
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Include significant paediatric trial findings, especially PIP safety objectives, in the PSUR
f.statement: Significant findings from paediatric clinical trials during the PSUR period should be included in the PSUR, especially when trials include safety objectives in an agreed, not yet completed PIP.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Present deferred PIP study information in PSURs due before paediatric development completes
f.statement: When a PSUR is due before the paediatric development agreed in a PIP is completed, all information on deferred clinical and non-clinical studies should be adequately presented.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force). Products with an agreed PIP not yet completed.

f.title: Consider long-term follow-up and registries for rare paediatric diseases with limited data
f.statement: For medicines for diseases rare in paediatric patients with lacking or very limited paediatric data, long-term follow-up and maintenance of registries documenting long-term outcomes should be considered by the MAH.
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Review deferred paediatric study programme at initial MAA for RMP inclusion
f.statement: The deferred paediatric clinical study programme in the PIP should be reviewed at the time of the initial marketing authorisation application so that specific safety objectives can be considered for inclusion in the RMP (part II, modules SVII and SVIII).
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).

f.title: Include PIP study results in EU marketing authorisation applications unless deferred or waived
f.statement: All applications for marketing authorisation for new medicines in the EU have to include results of studies described in an agreed PIP unless exempt by deferral or waiver; this also applies when adding a new indication, pharmaceutical form or route of administration for an authorised medicine covered by intellectual property rights.
f.clause: P.IV.B.6.2.3. Paediatric investigation plan in the EU (PIP)
f.applicability: Draft for public consultation (not in force).
f.exceptions: Medicines exempt because of a deferral or waiver.

f.statement: Children and their families in the EU can be consulted through established Young Person Advisory Groups (YPAG) for preparation of safety communication and educational materials for additional RMM.
